Official U.S. records of the November 23–24, 1974 SALT meeting between President Gerald R. Ford and L. I. Brezhnev (near Vladivostok) are published by the Gerald R. Ford Presidential Library and the Department of State Office of the Historian.
Public texts from the summit

    Joint U.S.–Soviet statement on strategic offensive arms (White House, Nov. 24, 1974)
    Joint U.S.–Soviet communiqué (White House, Nov. 24, 1974)
    SALT fact sheet on the Vladivostok understanding (NSC, Dec. 14, 1974)

Digitized files and finding aids

    Ford Library topic guide: Vladivostok Summit Meeting on Arms Control (includes a master list of digitized documents)
    Memoranda of conversation, Nov. 23, 1974 (Kissinger reports PDF)
    Memoranda of conversation, Nov. 24, 1974, and aide-mémoire (Kissinger reports PDF)
    Ron Nessen papers: SALT file with the joint statement and communiqué

State Department Foreign Relations volumes

    FRUS 1969–1976, Vol. XVI, Document 97 (aide-mémoire on SALT after Vladivostok)
    FRUS 1969–1976, Vol. XXXIII, Document 87 (summit overview)
    FRUS 1969–1976, Vol. XXXIII, Document 88 (memorandum of conversation, Nov. 24, 1974)
    FRUS 1969–1976, Vol. XXXIII, Document 89 (Soviet draft aide-mémoire)

The two-day meeting set a framework for a later SALT II agreement (equal ceilings of 2,400 strategic delivery vehicles and 1,320 MIRVed missiles). The formal SALT II treaty was not signed at Vladivostok.
